answers.question: Your inputs define no tools, so here is the smallest tool set in which every write has one call and every fact the agent needs before it acts has a read. Do you confirm it? (1) Look up the customer's orders: returns each of the signed-in customer's orders, cancelled ones included, each with its refund or none; or gets no answer. (2) Cancel an order, by order number: answers cancelled, answers rejected because the order has shipped, or gets no answer. Cancelling does not refund; the refund is its own call. (3) Refund an order, by order number: answers with a refund (amount, payment method, status pending, issued or failed), answers a temporary error with no refund made, or gets no answer. (4) Create a staff follow-up task, by order number and reason: the reasons are refund not issued, refund status unknown, cancellation unknown, and refund differs from what the customer agreed; answers created or gets no answer. Claims put to the owner: C-02, C-36.
answers.recommended: Yes, those four tools with those answers.
answers.reply:
> Proposed set shown to the user: list_orders() (returns each order with its refund or null), cancel_order(order_number), issue_refund(order_number) (supplied), request_staff_followup(order_number, reason) with reasons refund_not_issued, refund_status_unknown, cancellation_unknown; terminal refund error returns a refund with status failed, transient error creates none; handoff timeout not retried; SG-02 (store staff work every follow-up task) added.
> Confirmed, with four changes:
> 1. cancel_order is idempotent (cancelling a cancelled order returns cancelled). Outcomes: cancelled; OrderNotCancellable{status} (replaces OrderShipped, covers shipped and delivered); OrderNotFound; timeout.
> 2. issue_refund adds outcome OrderNotCancelled.
> 3. request_staff_followup is idempotent on (order_number, reason) — add as SG-03. On timeout, retry once; if it times out again, tell the customer to contact Harbor Goods support.
> 4. list_orders includes cancelled orders. Reads may be retried on timeout without limit; only commit calls are bounded.

answers.question: Your order system has no docs, so I compared it with common order systems. In those, a second refund call for an order that already has a refund either returns the existing refund or makes a second refund. The agent sends the refund call once more after a call with no answer. If your system returns the existing refund, that retry is safe and the agent goes on to re-read the order. If it could make a second refund, the agent should not retry after no answer and should re-read the order instead. Which holds? Claims put to the owner: C-24.
answers.recommended: A second refund call for an order that already has a refund returns that refund and makes no second one, so the agent's one retry is safe.
answers.reply:
> Tool contract: issue_refund(order_number) is idempotent, keyed on order number — repeated calls return the same refund id and never create a second refund. The store enforces this (supporting-actor guarantee, Appendix B). The agent may retry it.
> 3. Cancel succeeded, refund call timed out — state unknown; agent retries once, then re-reads the order and refund records and reports what it finds. Final message must match the final refund status.

answers.question: Your order system has no docs, so I compared it with common order systems. In those, a cancel call that gets no answer may still have cancelled the order. If that holds here, the agent cannot tell whether the order was cancelled. Under the recommendation the agent sends no second cancel call and no refund call, tells the customer it is not known whether the order was cancelled, and creates a staff follow-up task (cancellation unknown). Under the other answer, the agent would re-read the order and, if it shows cancelled, go on to the refund. Is that how your system behaves, and what should the agent do? Claims put to the owner: C-26, C-27.
answers.recommended: Yes: an unanswered cancel call may have cancelled the order. The agent sends no second cancel call and no refund call, tells the customer it is not known whether the order was cancelled, and creates a staff follow-up task.
answers.reply:
> Q4 If the cancel call times out: no blind resend; re-read the order. Cancelled, continue to refund. Still placed or processing, send the cancel once more under the same confirmation. Shipped, report it and issue no refund. Re-read fails, say outcome unknown, issue no refund, hand off.
> 1. cancel_order is idempotent (cancelling a cancelled order returns cancelled).
> Reads may be retried on timeout without limit; only commit calls are bounded.

answers.question: After a refund call with no answer and the one retry, the agent re-reads the order and its refund. When the re-read shows no refund, or the re-read itself gets no answer, the agent cannot tell what happened to the refund. What should it do? Claims put to the owner: C-32.
answers.recommended: It tells the customer the order is cancelled but it is not known whether the refund was issued, and creates a staff follow-up task (refund status unknown).
answers.reply:
> For case 3, after the retry the agent re-reads the refund record: pending or issued, report that status; failed or no refund, hand off and say the refund is not confirmed yet; re-read fails, say status unknown and hand off.
> 3. Cancel succeeded, refund call timed out — state unknown; agent retries once, then re-reads the order and refund records and reports what it finds. Final message must match the final refund status.
> Reads may be retried on timeout without limit; only commit calls are bounded.
